messages:
Ana: Heads up — canary for bb-model v4.0 with the new tokenizer just showed a p99 latency jump on a handful of hosts. Not all canaries, ~3/12 hosts. :eyes:
Ravi: link to dashboard?
Ana: https://grafana.internal/redwood/canary/34789 - see p99 from ~120ms -> 420ms after the canary push at 3478912200. It's correlated with increased kernel switches and cache misses.
Sophie: hmm noisy neighbor? which hosts?
Ana: hosts g-12, g-14, g-17. CPU on those hosts is normal, GPU util up modestly. KV cache hit rate on affected requests dropped from 92% -> 68%.
Matt: any tokenizer diffs that could change prefix alignment? new splitting rules?
Ana: yes, new tokenizer emits different leading subtoken for certain punctuation sequences — sample: "--foo" used to be single token, now two tokens. That shifts KV cache keys for many requests starting with markdown.
Joel: that would change kv_cache_id hash, so key miss -> cold KV chain -> more memory touches -> kernel selector sees longer seq/higher mem -> picks different kernel path.
Ravi: can you paste an example log from the runtime for an affected request?
Ana: pasted below:
```
[3478912235] REQUEST id=xyz123 tenant=acme model=bb-model:v4.0 seq_len=48 tokenizer_key=split_v4 kv_cache_id=hash:9f8a6b
[3478912235] KVCACHE lookup miss for prefix=markdown/--header
[3478912235] selected_kernel=streamed_quant_fallback latency_est=280ms
[3478912235] dispatch -> kernel conv_mixed_v2 (mem_prec=fp16, qpath=quant_cuda_fast)
[3478912235] actual_lat=412ms p99
```
Sophie: logger shows selected_kernel changed from conv_opt to conv_mixed_v2 on the miss. That lines up.
Matt: did the kernel-decider recent change include heuristics that consider kv_cache_hit_rate? We added a heuristic last month to prefer lower-memory kernels when cache hits low, to avoid thrashing right?
Ravi: yes we did, but IIRC it used a moving-average over the host, not per-tenant. If a noisy tenant causes bursty cache misses, the host-level avg may trigger kernel flips for other tenants too.
Joel: so this is a cross-tenant noisy neighbor amplified by tokenizer change altering cache keys. Two contributing factors.
Ana: repro steps I used: curl to /generate with payload that starts with markdown blockquote + code fence, repeated 60x to warm cache then switch to new tokenizer input -> observe drop. I left a replay trace in /tmp/replay_xyz123.trc.
Ravi: can we snapshot the KV entries for the sequence before/after? Need the hash mapping.
Sophie: I'll run a quick profiler and kv dump on g-14.
deploy-bot: Deploy canary bb-model:v4.0 -> hosts [g-12,g-14,g-17] at 3478912200 by @ana
Sophie: kv dump shows the old tokenizer had prefix key hash=0x7b12... now 0x9f8a6b... different entries, and host-level cache eviction rose due to slightly larger tokenization output leading to more kv objects per request.
Matt: action plan: 1) rollback canary on affected hosts -> reduce blast radius; 2) patch kernel-decider to consider tenant-level kv miss spikes before flipping kernel; 3) consider small tokenizer tweak to revert leading-subtoken change for punctuation sequences; 4) add canary watch that tracks kv hit delta per-host and abort rollout if >10pp drop.
Ana: I initiated rollback on g-12 and g-14. g-17 still under observation.
Ravi: I'll put a short-term guard in kernel-decider to require sustained drop >120s before switching kernels host-wide. That should be a quick config push.
Joel: For the longer term we should: add per-tenant cache miss metrics to the console, and change the kernel-decider to use stratified stats (tenant-aware) + more conservative thresholds.
Sophie: profiling shows the conv_mixed_v2 kernel had 2x L2 misses compared to conv_opt on these traces. Attaching flame outputs to the ticket.
Ana: ticket created: INF-6729 with logs and replay. Adding owners @ravi @sophie.
Matt: thumbs up. After rollback, p99 on those hosts fell back to baseline in ~90s. g-17 still noisy but no full regression yet.
Sophie: pushing kv-metrics dashboard panel now.
Ravi: config push for kernel-decider guard done; rolling out to canaries only.
Ana: update in 10m with g-17 status. Thanks all. :heart:
